t: Review and improve all 11 open/in_progress bug lugs for naming quality, PEV compliance, and self-containment
perceive: 1. ls WAI-Spoke/lugs/bytype/bug/open/*.json and WAI-Spoke/lugs/bytype/bug/in_progress/*.json — list all bug lugs. 2. Read each bug lug. 3. Check against quality standards: id matches filename, title is 5+ words and descriptive, has perceive/execute/verify fields, self-contained for cold reader.
execute: For each bug lug: 1. Read the full lug. 2. Check: (a) id = filename (without .json), (b) title is meaningful 5+ words, (c) has PEV fields, (d) description explains the bug clearly for a cold reader. 3. If any gap: rewrite the lug with improvements — add PEV if missing, expand title if vague, ensure description is self-contained. 4. Dogfood: spawn a sub-agent with just the lug content, ask 'What is this bug? How would you fix it? What would you check?' — if sub-agent can't answer, the lug needs more detail. 5. Write improved version back to the same path.
verify: 1. Every bug lug has: id matching filename, 5+ word title, perceive/execute/verify fields, description. 2. Dogfood sub-agent can explain what each bug is and how to verify the fix. 3. No lug has generic title like 'Bug: fix thing'.
acceptance_criteria: Every open/in_progress bug lug has: id matching filename, 5+ word title, perceive/execute/verify fields
Each bug description is self-contained for a cold reader
Dogfood sub-agent can explain what each bug is and how to verify the fix
Note: scope reduced from original 11 to current 2 open + 1 in_progress bugs

_behavior_directive.what_this_is: Batch review of all bug lugs for quality — the proof-of-concept batch for the lug quality epic
_behavior_directive.what_this_is_NOT: Not reviewing tasks, epics, or ideas — those are future batches
